title: EngineCapabilities
description: What the engine of a session can do, declared and never supposed (ADR-025). The client hides the controls of what the engine does not have, rather than disabling them: the engine will never have it. Per session, since the version of the binary or the model can change what holds; `GET /engines` gives the engine's before a session exists.

resume.description: A conversation can be continued where it stopped.

fork.description: A conversation can be forked at a message (edit-and-resend), whole, or not at all.

history.description: The conversations of a folder can be listed and read back.

promptWhileBusy.description: A prompt sent while a turn runs is queued.

questions.description: The agent asks the person a structured question.

planApproval.description: The agent asks for a plan to be approved before it acts.

taskList.description: The agent keeps a list of tasks the person can follow.

subagents.description: The agent delegates to subagents, whose work nests under the call.

thinking.description: The agent's reasoning streams as its own block.

slashCommands.description: The installation offers commands the composer lists.

modelSwitch.description: The model can be switched while the session lives.

effortLevels.description: The levels of effort the engine takes, in order — empty when it takes none.

contextUse.description: The use of the context window can be asked, by category.

mcp.description: MCP servers can be given to the session and their status read.

compaction.description: The conversation can be compacted on request.

cost.description: What a turn costs is reported, and in which unit — or not at all.

permissionModes.description: The canonical modes the engine runs in — what the clients offer, and nothing else. One mode only hides the selector.
